decisions.reason: Define-XML ADLBC.AVISIT states the full last-value flag method, including 'Y' at Visit 12, while its attached CL.AVISIT enumerates visit labels and excludes Y. Original MT.ADLBC.AVISIT (line 4836) and workbook Methods!D74 confirm that this is attached to AVISIT, so the documented conflict is real.

Define-XML ADLBC.PARAM states Concatenated LB.LBTEST, '(', LB.LBSTRESU and ')' with no separator, which the literal probe (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 112-116) concatenates exactly, and every reported difference is the missing space before the parenthesis. CL.PARAM_ADLBC in the same section shows that space, and the PARAM__CODELIST_SPACING reading reproduces the reference, as the finding reports.

Define-XML ADLBC.BASE gives Method: LB.LBSTNRHI as its single source, although the quote recorded here is blank. The reference BASE holds baseline analysis values, so it differs from LB.LBSTNRHI joined on STUDYID, USUBJID and LBSEQ as reported, and no ADLBC value-level metadata changes that source.

Define-XML ADLBC.CHG states AVAL - BASE with no baseline exception, and both the literal and CHG__UNROUNDED columns (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 165-179) give 0 where the reference CHG is missing. Those are the baseline records the specification blanks (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 381-384), so the difference follows from the rule, not from the declared precision.

Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1LO declares Significant digits: 1 for AVAL / A1LO, and the literal probe (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 180-190) applies that precision while the reference keeps unrounded ratios. The finding reports exactly this and that R2A1LO__UNROUNDED reproduces the reference, leaving the precision reading for a person to accept.

Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1HI declares Significant digits: 1 for AVAL / A1HI, and the literal probe (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 195-205) applies that precision while the reference keeps unrounded ratios. The finding reports exactly this and that R2A1HI__UNROUNDED reproduces the reference, leaving the precision reading for a person to accept.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1LO declares Significant digits: 1 for AVAL / A1LO at baseline, and the literal probe (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 210-231) takes the ABLFL='Y' ratio, identified by the cited ADLBC.ABLFL label, and applies that precision while the reference keeps unrounded values. The finding correctly reports that the unrounded baseline-ratio reading reproduces the reference.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1HI declares Significant digits: 1 for AVAL / A1HI at baseline, and the literal probe (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 251-272) takes the ABLFL='Y' ratio, identified by the cited ADLBC.ABLFL label, and applies that precision while the reference keeps unrounded values. The finding correctly reports that the unrounded baseline-ratio reading reproduces the reference.

Define-XML ADLBC.ANL01FL states If ALBTRVAL = max(ALBTRVAL) with no grouping, which the literal column (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 296-315) applies dataset-wide, and the subject/parameter reading drawn from ADRG page-8 still differs from the reference. The reference instead follows the visit-restricted, tie-broken ranking of adlbc_v1.yaml lines 302-316, so no reading of the documented rule reproduces it.

Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL states the maximum of LBSTRESN-(1.5*ULN) and (.5*LLN) - LBSTRESN, with ULN and LLN bound to A1HI and A1LO by the cited ADLBC.A1HI and ADLBC.A1LO methods. Both the rounded and unrounded columns (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 334-360) differ because the reference holds the sign-reversed differences, so the conflict does not depend on the precision reading.

The full Define-XML ADLBC.ANRIND method assigns Y for the low condition, while the same section's CL.LNH permits only L, N and H. Original MT.ADLBC.ANRIND (line 4830) and workbook Methods!D73 retain Y, so the conflict is not an extraction typo.

The literal probe (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 365-392) bounds 'during treatment phase' by ADT between TRTSDT and TRTEDT and orders the last assessment by ADT, yet no cited quote states either choice, and the cited ADSL.VISNUMEN label 'End of Trt Visit (Vis 12 or Early Term.)' points to a visit-based end of treatment instead. The mismatch therefore tests that added date boundary rather than Define-XML ADLBC.AENTMTFL as written; findings AENTMTFL.CR-6.1, CR-6.3 and CR-6.4 carry the real divergence.

Define-XML ADLBC.AVISIT's method (MT.ADLBC.AVISIT, define-adam.xml line 4836) assigns 'Y' if VISITNUM=12, while base-eot in adlbc_v1.yaml line 708 gives AVISIT the label 'End of Treatment' on the last Week 2 to Week 24 chemistry record by LBSEQ (lines 669 and 810-820). The assigned value differs, not only its wording, even though the documented method appears misplaced from AENTMTFL.

Define-XML ADLBC.ADY gives Method: LB.LBDY, but the specification computes ADY as study_day from _ADT_DATE and TRTSDT (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 327-333) and never reads LB.LBDY. The values agree with LB.LBDY on these data, which is the divergence CR-4 records.

Define-XML ADLBC.BASE names LB.LBSTNRHI, but the specification takes the ABLFL='Y' value of _AVAL_BASE (LB.LBSTRESN) carried forward within subject and parameter (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 587-606) and never reads LB.LBSTNRHI. The documented source is itself contradicted by the reference (BASE.CR-3), but the specification does not copy it, so CR-4 holds as stated.

Define-XML ADLBC.CHG states AVAL - BASE without exception, while the specification sets CHG missing when ABLFL = 'Y' (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 380-384). No retained section states that baseline-record exception, so the clause really differs.

base-ord copies A1LO: LB.LBSTNRLO directly (adlbc_v1.yaml line 478), and base-eot takes ONLY(LB.LBSTNRLO) within LB.USUBJID, LB.LBTESTCD and LB.LBSEQ (lines 665-668 and 689-690), which is a copy of the single LB record. The specification therefore reads the source Define-XML ADLBC.A1LO names, and the evidence shows no differing records.

base-ord copies A1HI: LB.LBSTNRHI directly (adlbc_v1.yaml line 479), and base-eot takes ONLY(LB.LBSTNRHI) within LB.USUBJID, LB.LBTESTCD and LB.LBSEQ (lines 665-668 and 691-692), which is a copy of the single LB record. The specification therefore reads the source Define-XML ADLBC.A1HI names, and the evidence shows no differing records.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1LO states AVAL / A1LO at baseline, while the specification divides _BASE by the current record's A1LO (adlbc_v1.yaml line 407), taking only the numerator from baseline. The computations differ whenever the lower limit changes after baseline, although the BR2A1LO.CR-5 readings show they agree on these data.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1HI states AVAL / A1HI at baseline, while the specification divides _BASE by the current record's A1HI (adlbc_v1.yaml line 412), taking only the numerator from baseline. The computations differ whenever the upper limit changes after baseline, although the BR2A1HI.CR-5 readings show they agree on these data.

Define-XML ADLBC.ANL01FL flags every record whose ALBTRVAL equals the maximum, while the specification flags _ANL01_RANK = 1 (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 419-420), a rank within subject and parameter restricted to AVISITN 2 to 24 and ordered by visit, date and LBSEQ (lines 302-316). Tied maxima after the first-ranked record and records outside those visits are treated differently, so the clause differs.

Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL states LBSTRESN-(1.5*ULN), while base-ord computes _T1 as 1.5 * A1HI - _AVAL_BASE (adlbc_v1.yaml line 618, repeated in base-eot at line 844), the reverse sign. The ALBTRVAL.CR-5 evidence confirms the reference follows the reversed form, so this is a real difference.

Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL states (.5*LLN) - LBSTRESN, while base-ord computes _T2 as _AVAL_BASE - 0.5 * A1LO (adlbc_v1.yaml line 619, repeated in base-eot at line 845), the reverse sign. The ALBTRVAL.CR-5 evidence confirms the reference follows the reversed form, so this is a real difference.

Define-XML ADLBC.ANRIND assigns 'Y' when AVAL < 0.5*LBSTNRLO, while base-ord assigns 'L' when _R2A1LO_R < 0.5 (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 635-636). The threshold corresponds but the assigned code differs; that Y also conflicts with CL.LNH is the separate CR-8.3 finding.

Define-XML ADLBC.ANRIND assigns 'H' when AVAL > [0.5*LBSTRNHI), while base-ord assigns 'H' when AVAL / A1HI exceeds 1.5 (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 633-634) and tests it before the low branch. The multiplier, source name and order all differ, so the specification does not express the documented clause.

Define-XML ADLBC.BNRIND compares BASE with 0.5*LBSTNRLO and 0.5*LBSTRNHI, while the specification carries the baseline record's _ANRIND_BASE forward by LBSEQ within subject and parameter (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 638-656). That propagates the baseline record's 1.5 and 0.5 ratio tests and L code rather than the documented comparison, and leaves records before baseline without a value.

Define-XML ADLBC.AENTMTFL conditions the last-assessment case on the subject discontinuing before Visit 12, but AENTMTFL (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 437-446), _IS_LAST_ELIGIBLE (lines 607-616) and base-eot read no discontinuation source. Neither adlbc_v3.yaml nor the entry adds one beyond the copied method description, so the condition has no executable counterpart.

Define-XML ADLBC.AENTMTFL selects the last assessment of the analyte, while _IS_LAST_ELIGIBLE takes the highest LBSEQ among eligible records (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 607-616). LBSEQ is a sequence number, not an assessment date or time, so the specification states a different ordering source.

Define-XML ADLBC.AVISIT (MT.ADLBC.AVISIT, line 4836) carries the AENTMTFL flag text, which yields 'Y' rather than a visit label, and CL.AVISIT and ADRG page-8 give only the allowed labels and an AVISITN=99 end-of-treatment visit. No retained section states the visit-to-label mapping, the baseline or unscheduled handling, or how the End of Treatment record is selected, so a literal probe cannot be written.

The ADLBC.VISITNUM section text omits Origin, so CR-11's absence premise is wrong; the one-decimal rounding adlbc_v3.yaml lines 555-558 adds is a clause question, not a missing derivation.

Define-XML ADLBC.ANL01FL states only equality to max(ALBTRVAL), and neither ADRG page-8 nor any other retained section restricts the search to analysis visits Week 2 to Week 24. The _ANL01_RANK filter (adlbc_v1.yaml line 316) therefore has no documented counterpart.

Define-XML ADLBC.ANL01FL gives only equality to max(ALBTRVAL), and no retained section states a tie-break for the flag. The _ANL01_RANK ordering by _RANK_AVISITN, _ADT_DATE and LBSEQ (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 313-315) is therefore undocumented.

Define-XML ADLBC.ANRIND ends with ,'H','N', so N is the documented fallback when neither threshold test assigns a code, which is exactly the quoted otherwise branch (adlbc_v1.yaml line 637). The missing-AVAL behaviour the note raises comes from the null ratio tests, not from an undocumented N branch.

Define-XML ADLBC.ANRIND names LBSTRNHI, which neither the staged LB nor define-sdtm.xml holds (LB has LBSTNRHI), writes unbalanced brackets with a 0.5 upper multiplier, and assigns Y, which CL.LNH in the same section excludes. A literal probe needs repairs that no retained section or ADLBC value-level metadata supplies.

Define-XML ADLBC.BNRIND always ends in an H or N choice and states no empty-string result for a missing baseline indicator. ADRG page-36 compares Dataset-JSON missing-value representations in general, not this rule, so the BNRIND empty-string branch (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 433-434) is undocumented.

Define-XML ADLBC.BNRIND assigns ANRIND rather than BNRIND, names LBSTRNHI, which the staged LB lacks (it has LBSTNRHI), and gives the low code Y that CL.LNH in the same section excludes. No retained section resolves the target, source and threshold, so the rule cannot be probed as written.

Original spec/define/define-adam.xml IT.ADLBC.ABLFL has def:Origin Type Predecessor naming LB.LBBLFL (lines 1755-1759), and workbook Variables row 138 repeats it. The ADLBC.ABLFL section text omits Origin, so the finding's premise that no retained document states this derivation is wrong.

Define-XML ADLBC.AENTMTFL, repeated under ADLBC.AVISIT, bounds the candidates only as the treatment phase with VISITNUM=12 as its scheduled end, and ADRG page-5 says unscheduled visits were used in analyses; no section, including ADRG page-8, lists the Week 2 to Week 24 scheduled visits or excludes unscheduled ones. The VISIT filter on _IS_LAST_ELIGIBLE (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 615-616, kept in the resolved specification) therefore has no documented counterpart.

Original spec/define/define-adam.xml IT.ADLBC.LBSEQ has def:Origin Type Predecessor naming LB.LBSEQ (lines 1773-1777), and workbook Variables row 140 repeats it. The ADLBC.LBSEQ section text omits Origin, so the finding's premise that no retained document states this derivation is wrong.

Original spec/define/define-adam.xml IT.ADLBC.LBNRIND has def:Origin Type Predecessor naming LB.LBNRIND (lines 1785-1789), and workbook Variables row 141 repeats it. The ADLBC.LBNRIND section text omits Origin, so the finding's premise that no retained document states this derivation is wrong.

Original spec/define/define-adam.xml IT.ADLBC.LBSTRESN has def:Origin Type Predecessor naming LB.LBSTRESN (lines 1797-1801), and workbook Variables row 142 repeats it. The ADLBC.LBSTRESN section text omits Origin, so the finding's premise that no retained document states this derivation is wrong.

Define-XML ADLBC.PARAM builds the label by concatenating LB.LBTEST and LB.LBSTRESU, while the specification maps LB.LBTESTCD to fixed labels in base-ord (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 541-563) and repeats them as a case on _LBTESTCD in base-eot (lines 711-749). The source and computation differ even though the fixed labels match the CL.PARAM_ADLBC values.

Define-XML ADLBC.AENTMTFL assigns 'Y' when VISITNUM=12, but AENTMTFL (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 441-446) flags every End of Treatment row and the last eligible record by LBSEQ, with no VISITNUM test. A Week 24 record is flagged only when it is that last eligible record, so the clause differs.

Define-XML ADLBC.ANRIND compares AVAL with 0.5*LBSTNRLO and says nothing about a missing or zero lower limit, and no other retained section does. The _R2A1LO_R guard that leaves the ratio missing for such limits (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 626-630) is therefore undocumented.

Define-XML ADLBC.AVISIT gives only the misplaced flag method and CL.AVISIT's allowed labels, and ADRG page-5 (section 3.3) and page-8 say only that windowing was used somewhere and that an end-of-treatment visit is derived. No retained section maps LB.VISIT to the base-ord labels of adlbc_v3.yaml lines 528-550, takes Baseline from SCREENING 1 (CL.VISIT also lists a BASELINE visit), or leaves an unscheduled visit blank.

missed.reason: The ADRG page-7 dataset table gives ADLBC as one or more records per subject per analysis parameter per analysis timepoint, a record-scope statement for base-ord and its base-eot rows that no claim cites. It differs from the one-record wording on ADRG page-8 and from the entry specification's structure line, so a person should reconcile them.
